name: Yevgeniy Vorobeychik
title: Professor
fitReason: Relevant safe embodied-agent match through conformal LLM planning and reliability research. His broader group spans security, game theory and AI beyond robotics, so a robot-specific project and collaborator access should be checked.

physicalEvidence.summary: CoFineLLM, published at L4DC 2026, demonstrates its finetuned LLM plans on a TurtleBot3 Waffle-Pi with OpenManipulator-X in a miniature urban scene. The full preprint explicitly separates this physical demonstration from its 80 generated out-of-distribution validation scenarios. First author Jun Wang identifies Yiannis Kantaros as his doctoral adviser, so the hardware is treated as collaborative rather than verified independently accessible Vorobeychik-lab equipment.

shortVisit.summary: The official Summer 2026 International Student Research Internship Program names Vorobeychik and trustworthy-autonomy projects, but it requires full-time penultimate-year bachelor’s enrollment abroad. Its November 13, 2025 deadline and ten-week funding terms do not establish a master’s pathway or Summer 2027 opening. No separate current external-master’s invitation was verified.

name: Hongrui Yu
school: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
title: Assistant Professor
department: Charles E. Via, Jr. Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering; Vecellio Construction Engineering and Management Program
fitReason: Strong applied embodied-AI match combining construction skill learning, LLM-driven interaction and multimodal perception. Current work includes VLA/HRL benchmarking, but physical evidence must be separated from simulator results and earlier Michigan collaborations.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full 2025 Generalizable Skill Learning preprint establishes actual industrial-manipulator drywall execution in a Michigan collaboration. LLM-derived elemental actions and learned skill chaining are followed by explicit human approval; approved sequences trigger ROS and programmed Python motion functions (§4.2). This is supervised hybrid execution, not autonomous closed-loop VLA, and is not verified current VT industrial-robot inventory. The separate i3CE interaction paper explicitly reports a Reactor RX200 physical validation on p6, but provides limited action-level detail and leaves expanded physical urban/ROS embodiment to future work on p7; its photo and brief statement are treated as a limited prototype report, not a quantified learned-policy deployment.

shortVisit.summary: Reviewed official and personal research pages provide a public professional contact and local graduate-student collaboration, but no current outside-master’s, summer-intern or short-visit invitation was verified. The September 2026 institutional construction-robotics initiative corroborates active Virginia Tech research, not visitor intake.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct embodied learning, language interaction and construction manipulation, with VLA work currently simulation-based.
scoreReasons.physical: Verified supervised industrial robot execution in Michigan collaboration; current VT RX200 prototype only briefly reported and not counted as a fully documented learned-policy deployment.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: No lab-specific current external-master’s short-visit invitation.
scoreReasons.freshness: 2026 publication record/current university initiative plus fully reviewed recent papers.

The full interaction paper names Reactor RX200, while the PI portfolio names RX250. Preserve this model discrepancy. The methods establish classifier finetuning and prompted LLM command generation, not verified reinforcement learning from human feedback of a robot policy.

Classifier accuracy is not robot task success. The interaction paper reports overfitting and degraded skewed-avatar-view performance. Its p6 RX200 validation statement and p7 physical-embodiment future-work wording must both be retained. Physical credit is capped at 20, resting on verified collaborative industrial execution rather than an assumed fully integrated RX200 policy.
The shared Sample-Efficient Robot Skill Learning VLA/HRL paper explicitly runs all evaluation in MuJoCo (§5.1). Its 60%/100% pickup numbers are simulator results, not real UR5e/Franka execution.

The full Generalizable Skill Learning paper has a human approve action sequences and uses conventional motion planning. Its industrial manipulator is a Michigan collaboration, not verified current VT KUKA inventory.
